lines.say: Your friend hit send, and it popped up on your phone instantly.

lines.say: You never refreshed. So how did your app know?

lines.say: Normally, your app asks the server a question, and the server answers. Want an update? Ask again.
lines.show: Normally, your app *asks* the server a question, and the server *answers.* Want an update? [Ask again.]

lines.say: In that setup, the server only speaks when asked.
lines.show: In that setup, the server only speaks *when asked.*

lines.say: A WebSocket keeps a line open between them, like a phone call nobody hangs up.
lines.show: A [WebSocket] keeps a line open between them, like a *phone call* nobody hangs up.

lines.say: Now either side can talk any time. When your friend's message reaches the server, it sends it straight down the line to you.
lines.show: Now *either side* can talk any time. When your friend's message reaches the server, it sends it [straight down the line] to you.

lines.say: One catch. Every open line uses server memory, and if the connection breaks, your app has to reconnect.
lines.show: One catch. Every open line uses *server memory,* and if the connection breaks, your app has to [reconnect.]

lines.say: Discord uses WebSockets for live updates, and modern browsers support them.
lines.show: *Discord* uses WebSockets for live updates, and modern *browsers* support them.
